summary: Pitchbook tables should be hand-built: a small in-house RK.Table and RK.Sensitivity component (DOM <table>, CSS tokens, inline-SVG micro-charts). Comps, precedents, financial summaries and sensitivity tables are static, dense, under 500 cells and typeset to bank conventions: phantom-parenthesis decimal alignment, NM/NA rules, x and % suffixes, underlined group headers, a target row excluded from Mean/Median/High/Low rows, footnotes. Every grid library fights these details, while a DOM table prints as vectors, repeats headers on each page, pastes into Excel/PowerPoint and works with Ctrl+F at zero dependency cost. For large, interactive or editable lists, adopt Tabulator 6.6.1 (MIT, UMD tabulator.min.js, ~103 KB gz, DOM). It covers frozen columns, nested headers, groupBy with group calcs, range selection and fill handle, printAsHtml and CSV/XLSX/PDF download. Gotchas: only one top and one bottom calc per column, built-in calcs return strings, and XLSX output is unstyled. AG Grid Community 36.2.0 (MIT, ~522 KB gz) is the runner-up; it has multi-row pinnedBottomRowData for stats rows, column groups and pinning, but grouping, aggregation, pivot, Excel export, sparklines, clipboard, range selection and formulas are Enterprise ($999/dev). For an optional, lazy-loaded pivot or cross-tab data explorer, adopt AntV S2 2.7.2 (MIT, UMD ~310 KB gz, canvas). It has totals and subtotals, tree mode, conditions (background, interval bars, icons), built-in line/bar/bullet mini charts and copy/export, but defaults to Chinese labels unless S2.setLang('en_US') is called. VisActor VTable 1.26.8 is the heavier alternative (~544 KB gz plus ~358 KB gz of plugins); it adds sparkline and progress-bar cells, pivot charts and a built-in appear animation. Never use canvas grids for the primary printed tables. Headless Chromium tests confirmed that Tabulator, AG Grid, S2, VTable, DataTables 3 (now jQuery-free), Grid.js, Cheetah Grid, SlickGrid (needs SortableJS) and write-excel-file all work from file://. Perspective (now @perspective-dev 5.6.0, Apache-2.0; ESM + WASM loaded via import.meta.url) fails with a CORS error, so keep it for a Step-2 served mode, where its ExprTK expression columns fit client-typed formulas. For styled XLSX export use write-excel-file 4.1.1 (MIT, ~19 KB gz: number formats, fills, borders, merges, frozen panes, formulas). For reading client files use SheetJS CE 0.20.3 from cdn.sheetjs.com only, because npm xlsx@0.18.5 has CVE-2023-30533 and CVE-2024-22363. Use browser print CSS for PDF. Avoid Grid.js (stale), Glide (React-only, stale), RevoGrid (Stencil ESM; export and pivot are Pro), PivotTable.js (jQuery, 2018), simple-datatables (LGPL), HyperFormula (GPL) and WebDataRocks (EULA, ~1 MB cap). Handsontable, Flexmonster and AG Grid Enterprise are reference only. Define tables with a declarative JSON TableSpec (columns, formats, NM rules, stats, heat, sparkline cells, expression columns). It renders through RK.Table and can be adapted to Tabulator, AG Grid or S2, and it gives the future local LLM a safe, code-free target.

libraries.name: Hand-built RK.Table / RK.Sensitivity / rk.spark (in-house)
libraries.capabilities: Pitchbook comps, precedent, sensitivity, financial-summary and league tables. Multi-level headers with gapped underlines; sticky header and first column; bank number formats (x, %, $, parentheses, NM/NA/en dash, phantom paren); target row highlight; tfoot Mean/Median/High/Low/percentile rows excluding the target; peer-group sections; opt-in heat colouring; inline SVG sparkline, two-sided data bar, bullet and 52-week range cells; CSV/XLSX export; print CSS.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: Cell fill colour (sequential or diverging heat), bar length from a zero axis, sparkline position, dot on a range track, icon or arrow direction, bold or tint for row role
libraries.interactions_animation: Sort with stats rows pinned (FLIP row reorder via WAAPI); filter chips and cross-filter via RK.bus; cross-fade of recomputed stats; data bars grow on reveal; prefers-reduced-motion respected; no motion in print
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: own IIFE classic script on window.RK, no dependencies
libraries.reason: Bank tables are small, static and tightly typeset. A DOM table gives vector print, repeated headers, copy into Excel/PPT, Ctrl+F and a11y, with zero licence surface. Libraries fight the typesetting details.

libraries.name: Tabulator
libraries.capabilities: Interactive DOM grid with virtual DOM. Frozen columns and rows, nested column groups, header filters, multi-sort, groupBy with group calcs, top and bottom column calcs (avg/sum/min/max/count/custom), dataTree, clipboard, history, range selection, fill handle (6.6), spreadsheet mode, pagination, persistence. Download as CSV/JSON/HTML/XLSX (via SheetJS) or PDF (via jsPDF + AutoTable); print module with printAsHtml.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: Via formatters: progress bars, colour cells, custom SVG sparklines; row and cell styling by value
libraries.interactions_animation: Sorting, filtering, grouping, editing, column move and resize; no built-in animation
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/js/tabulator.min.js (UMD, global Tabulator, all modules) + dist/css/tabulator_simple.min.css; verified under file:// in headless Chromium
libraries.reason: Best mix of MIT licence, classic script, DOM rendering (print, copy, a11y) and rich features for large or editable lists. Limits: one top and one bottom calc per column; built-in calcs return strings; XLSX output is unstyled; must use printAsHtml for printing.

libraries.name: AG Grid Community
libraries.capabilities: High-performance virtualised grid. Column groups, column pinning, pinned top and bottom rows (multiple), sorting and filtering, cell renderers, CSV export, undo/redo, basic editors, domLayout:'print'. Grouping, aggregation, pivot, tree data, Excel export, sparklines, clipboard, range selection, formulas, calculated columns, Find and the status bar are Enterprise only.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: cellClassRules / cellStyle for conditional colours; custom cellRenderer for SVG bars and sparklines (native sparklines are Enterprise)
libraries.interactions_animation: Row and column animations, sort and filter, column move and resize
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/ag-grid-community.min.js (UMD, global agGrid, auto-registers Community modules, CSS-in-JS themes); verified under file://
libraries.reason: Most polished grid for 100k+ rows, and multi-row pinnedBottomRowData is ideal for stats rows. But it is heavy, and the features that matter (grouping, aggregation, Excel export, sparklines) are paywalled. Use it as an alternative to Tabulator.

libraries.name: AG Grid Enterprise
libraries.capabilities: Adds row grouping, aggregation, pivoting, tree data, master/detail, set, multi and advanced filters, Excel export, clipboard, range selection, fill handle, sparklines, formulas, calculated columns (v36), Find, status bar, tool panels; integrated charts in the Bundle
libraries.offline_classic_script: UMD exists but needs a licence key; shows a watermark and console error without one
libraries.reason: Commercial licence is not allowed in open client deliverables; reference only for feature benchmarking.

libraries.name: AntV S2
libraries.capabilities: Canvas pivot and cross-tab (PivotSheet) and detail (TableSheet) tables. Rows, columns and values fields; grid and tree hierarchy; drill-down; grand totals and subtotals (SUM/MIN/MAX/AVG/COUNT/custom calcFunc); sort by measure; frozen rows and columns; merge cells; editable mode; copy with format and headers; asyncGetAllPlainData for CSV
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: conditions: text colour, background fill, interval (in-cell bar with custom range), icons; built-in mini charts (line, bar, bullet) without G2; full G2 charts in cells optional
libraries.interactions_animation: Brush selection, hover and row/column highlight, resize, collapse and expand, scrolling; little animation
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/s2.min.js (UMD, global S2) + dist/s2.min.css; verified under file://. Default locale zh_CN, so call S2.setLang('en_US').
libraries.reason: Best open-source cross-tab engine, lighter than VTable. Use only as an optional, lazy-loaded data-explorer module, never for printed primary tables (canvas).

libraries.name: VisActor VTable
libraries.capabilities: Canvas ListTable (tree, group, transpose), PivotTable, PivotChart (with VChart), Gantt, Calendar, VTable-Sheet with formulas. Aggregation (SUM/AVG/MAX/MIN/COUNT/CUSTOM), frozen left, right and bottom, conditional style functions, themes, custom render; export via @visactor/vtable-plugins TableExportPlugin (ExcelJS-based); exportImg
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: sparkline cells (line), progressbar cells, chart cells (any VChart spec), conditional bg and text colours, icons
libraries.interactions_animation: animationAppear (one-by-one by row or column), scroll and carousel animation, drag headers, resize, select, edit, fill handle
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/vtable.min.js (UMD, global VTable); plugins at dist/vtable-plugins.min.js; verified under file:// (container size must be integers)
libraries.reason: Broadest MIT canvas table with in-cell charts and entry animation, but the heaviest option. Canvas limits print, copy and a11y. Pick it instead of S2 only if one canvas engine must cover list, pivot and in-cell charts.

libraries.name: Perspective (@perspective-dev)
libraries.capabilities: Streaming WASM (C++) query engine with group-by and split-by pivots, ExprTK expression columns, reactive joins, virtual servers (DuckDB, ClickHouse), Python/Node/Rust hosts; perspective-viewer custom element with datagrid and WebGL charts. The old @finos/perspective scope is frozen at 3.8.0.
libraries.multi_dim_encoding: Datagrid colour modes (bars, gradients), d3fc/WebGL charts, maps
libraries.interactions_animation: Drag-and-drop pivot configuration, real-time ticking updates
libraries.offline_classic_script: No: dist/cdn/*.js are ES modules with top-level await, and they fetch .wasm via import.meta.url. Failed with a CORS error under file:// in headless Chromium.
libraries.size: viewer ~25 KB gz JS + ~1.6 MB WASM, plus client ~0.6 MB WASM
libraries.reason: Best engine for big or streaming pivots with user formulas, but incompatible with double-click file:// reports. Plan it for Step-2 served mode.

libraries.name: DataTables
libraries.capabilities: Progressive enhancement of an existing HTML <table>: sort, search, paging, footerCallback. v3 (2026-07) is dependency-free (no jQuery) and ported to TypeScript. MIT extensions: FixedColumns 6.1.1, FixedHeader 5.1.2, RowGroup 2.1.1, Buttons 4.1.2 (CSV, Excel via JSZip, PDF via pdfmake, print), ColumnControl 2.1.2, SearchPanes
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: js/dataTables.min.js (UMD, window.DataTable); verified under file:// with no jQuery loaded
libraries.reason: Good fit for enhancing Python-rendered static tables, but its look is opinionated and it has no median or percentile calcs. Our own enhancer covers the same in a few KB.

libraries.name: Grid.js
libraries.capabilities: Simple table with search, sort, pagination and server-side data
libraries.reason: No release since 2024-03; no frozen columns, grouping or calcs. The hand-built table covers more.

libraries.name: TanStack Table
libraries.capabilities: Headless table state: row models for sort, filter, group, aggregate, expand and paginate; v9 adds a plugin and feature system on TanStack Store, cell (range) selection, cell spanning and 10 framework adapters
libraries.offline_classic_script: v9: no (ESM-only, type:module). v8.21.3 ships build/umd/index.production.js (~15 KB gz).
libraries.reason: Excellent architecture reference for RK.Table state and row models; the v9 dependency is not usable as a classic script and is not needed.

libraries.name: Handsontable
libraries.license: Proprietary (dual; non-commercial key 'non-commercial-and-evaluation'; commercial requires a paid key)
libraries.capabilities: Excel-like spreadsheet grid with formulas (HyperFormula), merged cells, nested headers, filters, export
libraries.reason: Commercial licence for business use (single 90-day non-production evaluation); not allowed in client deliverables.

libraries.name: HyperFormula
libraries.capabilities: Headless Excel-compatible formula engine
libraries.reason: GPL-3.0 copyleft is incompatible with the policy. Use in-house rk.expr plus formulajs (MIT) instead.

libraries.name: RevoGrid
libraries.capabilities: Virtualised web-component grid: grouping, sorting, pinning, editing; Pro adds Excel export and import, pivot, formulas, charts and cell merge
libraries.offline_classic_script: No UMD: Stencil ESM lazy chunks (dist/revo-grid/*.esm.js) and a CJS loader. Not file://-friendly without bundling.
libraries.reason: ESM web components break the file:// requirement, and the key features (Excel export, pivot) are commercial Pro.

libraries.name: Glide Data Grid
libraries.capabilities: Canvas React data grid for millions of rows with custom cell renderers
libraries.reason: React-only. Stable release stale since 2024-02 (alpha 2025-10).

libraries.name: SlickGrid (6pac)
libraries.capabilities: Very fast virtualised grid: frozen columns and rows, column groups (pre-header), DataView grouping with Avg/Sum/Min/Max/custom aggregators, editors, plugins (copy manager, header menus)
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/browser/slick.core.js + slick.interactions.js + slick.dataview.js + slick.grid.js (IIFE); requires the SortableJS global; verified under file://
libraries.reason: Lean and fast, but the API and look are dated, and XLSX export lives in the separate slickgrid-universal ESM ecosystem. Tabulator is friendlier.

libraries.name: Cheetah Grid
libraries.capabilities: Fast canvas list grid with multi-level headers, frozen columns, column types and actions
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/main.umd.js (global cheetahGrid) + dist/main.css; verified under file://
libraries.reason: Light and fast, but canvas limits print, copy and a11y, and it has no aggregation or pivot. Not needed given Tabulator and S2.

libraries.name: canvas-datagrid
libraries.capabilities: Canvas spreadsheet-like data grid
libraries.reason: Niche canvas grid; canvas print and a11y limits; nothing unique for reports.

libraries.name: Frappe DataTable
libraries.capabilities: Simple editable DOM data table with inline filters and tree rows
libraries.reason: Tied to the Frappe ecosystem; offers nothing beyond Tabulator.

libraries.name: simple-datatables
libraries.capabilities: Vanilla DataTables-like sort, search and paging
libraries.reason: LGPL-3.0 is outside the permissive-licence policy.

libraries.name: PivotTable.js
libraries.capabilities: Drag-and-drop pivot UI with aggregators and renderers (table, heatmap, bar chart, C3/D3 charts)
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: dist/pivot.min.js but requires jQuery + jQuery UI
libraries.reason: Unmaintained since 2018 and needs jQuery + jQuery UI. Keep only as a UX reference for a future pivot builder.

libraries.name: react-pivottable
libraries.capabilities: React port of the PivotTable.js UI
libraries.reason: React-only; does not fit the vanilla classic-script kit.

libraries.name: WebDataRocks
libraries.license: Proprietary EULA (free; OEM/SaaS redistribution prohibited; not OSI)
libraries.capabilities: Free pivot table UI with conditional formatting, number formats, export and chart integrations; data capped at ~1 MB
libraries.reason: Non-OSI proprietary licence, ~1 MB data cap, stale since 2023.

libraries.name: Flexmonster
libraries.capabilities: Enterprise pivot (OLAP, large data, SQL/NoSQL connectors), export, conditional formatting
libraries.reason: Commercial; reference for pivot UX only.

libraries.name: Jspreadsheet CE
libraries.license: MIT (LICENSE file; npm license field blank)
libraries.capabilities: Lightweight spreadsheet UI with basic formulas, editing, copy/paste
libraries.reason: Only relevant if clients must type formulas into a grid (Step 2 what-if sheets); formula columns via rk.expr are lighter.

libraries.name: Univer
libraries.capabilities: Full canvas spreadsheet and doc suite with a formula engine, multi-sheet, collaboration
libraries.offline_classic_script: Per-package lib/umd/index.js (core alone ~490 KB raw; many packages)
libraries.reason: Permissive and powerful, but far too heavy for report tables. Keep for a possible Step-2 what-if workbook.

libraries.name: Formula.js
libraries.capabilities: JS implementations of Excel functions (statistical, financial NPV/XNPV/IRR/XIRR/PMT, math, text, date)
libraries.reason: Optional Excel-parity function catalogue behind the in-house rk.expr evaluator for client-typed metrics; the MIT alternative to HyperFormula.

libraries.name: SheetJS Community Edition
libraries.capabilities: Read and write XLSX/XLS/CSV/ODS; values, number formats, merges; no cell fills or fonts in CE (Pro feature). Required by Tabulator's XLSX download.
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: xlsx.mini.min.js (~86 KB gz) or xlsx.full.min.js (~334 KB gz) from cdn.sheetjs.com
libraries.reason: Best reader for client-supplied spreadsheets. Must come from cdn.sheetjs.com 0.20.3: npm 0.18.5 has CVE-2023-30533 and CVE-2024-22363.

libraries.name: write-excel-file
libraries.capabilities: Write styled XLSX: number formats, fonts, text colour, background fills, per-side borders, alignment, wrap, rotation, column and row spans, formulas, column widths, frozen rows and columns, orientation, images
libraries.offline_classic_script: Yes: bundle/write-excel-file.min.js (UMD, global writeXlsxFile; v4 API writeXlsxFile(data,opts).toBlob()); verified under file://
libraries.reason: Tiny MIT library that exports pitchbook-formatted XLSX (x/%/parentheses formats, bold stats rows, fills, frozen panes), which SheetJS CE cannot.

libraries.name: ExcelJS
libraries.capabilities: Full XLSX read/write with styles, native conditional-formatting rules, data validation, images; used by VTable's export plugin
libraries.reason: Use only if real Excel conditional-format rules or template editing are required; heavy and slow-moving (last release 2023).

libraries.name: xlsx-js-style
libraries.capabilities: Fork of SheetJS 0.18 that writes cell styles
libraries.reason: Stale since 2022 and inherits the SheetJS 0.18 CVEs; write-excel-file covers styled export.

libraries.name: jsPDF + jsPDF-AutoTable
libraries.capabilities: Programmatic PDF generation; AutoTable draws tables; Tabulator's PDF download depends on them (its docs pin jsPDF 2.4 + AutoTable 3.5.20)
libraries.reason: Only for a no-dialog 'Download PDF' button. Browser print CSS (or headless Chrome in the Python builder) gives better pitchbook fidelity.

libraries.name: SortableJS
libraries.capabilities: Drag-and-drop reordering; required by SlickGrid 5 column reorder
libraries.reason: Needed only if SlickGrid is chosen; could also power column or row reordering in RK.Table.

libraries.name: Observable Inputs (Inputs.table)
libraries.capabilities: Minimal, elegant sortable table input with tabular numbers and sticky header
libraries.reason: Good typographic reference for a clean, dense numeric table; not needed as a dependency.

key_insights: Split tables into three layers. (1) Hand-built RK.Table for printed pitchbook tables (comps, precedents, sensitivities). (2) Tabulator for large or editable interactive lists. (3) Lazy-loaded S2 (or VTable) for pivot exploration. Canvas grids never carry primary printed tables.

Verified under file:// in headless Chromium 141: Tabulator, AG Grid CE, S2, VTable, DataTables 3, Grid.js, Cheetah Grid, SlickGrid (with SortableJS) and write-excel-file all work as classic scripts. Perspective 5.6.0 fails because it is ESM with top-level await and fetches WASM via import.meta.url.

On file://, fetch() of local files fails, but window.isSecureContext is true, navigator.clipboard exists and Blob plus <a download> works. Ship data as data/*.js (window.__RK_DATA__) or inline <script type=application/json>. Copy and download buttons work offline.

Tabulator gotchas: only one topCalc and one bottomCalc per column, so Mean, Median, High and Low need tfoot, a separate stats table or pinned synthetic rows. Built-in calcs return precision-formatted strings. XLSX download is unstyled (SheetJS CE). Printing needs printAsHtml or only the virtual viewport prints.

AG Grid Community does include multi-row pinnedBottomRowData (ideal for stats rows), column groups, pinning, CSV and print layout. Grouping, aggregation, pivot, Excel export, sparklines, clipboard, range selection, formulas and calculated columns are Enterprise ($999/dev). Vendor only ag-grid-community to avoid a watermark or licence breach.

AntV S2 defaults to Chinese labels ('总计' for grand total), so call S2.setLang('en_US'). Its conditions API (text, background, interval, icon with a regex field) and built-in line/bar/bullet mini charts map well to bank heat tables.

VTable: container size must be integer pixels; aggregation rows need bottomFrozenRowCount; @visactor/vtable-export is deprecated in favour of vtable-plugins TableExportPlugin (ExcelJS-based, +358 KB gz). animationAppear (one-by-one by row or column) is a good model for tasteful table entry motion.

Perspective moved npm scope from @finos (frozen at 3.8.0) to @perspective-dev (5.6.0, repo perspective-dev/perspective). Its ExprTK expression columns and DuckDB virtual servers suit the future client-formula, served-mode step.
DataTables 3.0 (2026-07-22) dropped jQuery; the UMD dataTables.min.js sets window.DataTable. It is a viable progressive enhancer for Python-rendered static tables.
Never npm install xlsx: 0.18.5 is the last npm version and carries CVE-2023-30533 and CVE-2024-22363. Get SheetJS CE 0.20.3 from cdn.sheetjs.com. CE writes no fills or fonts.

write-excel-file 4.1.1 (MIT, ~19 KB gz, UMD global writeXlsxFile) exports styled XLSX: Excel number formats such as 0.0"x" and #,##0.0_);(#,##0.0), fills, per-side borders, spans, formulas and frozen panes. The v4 API is writeXlsxFile(...).toBlob()/.toFile().

Pitchbook typesetting conventions: right-aligned tabular figures; a phantom ')' on positives so decimals align with '(3.4)'; x and % suffixes; NM for negative or >100x multiples; NA; en dash for zero; target row tinted and excluded from stats; bold stats rows after a rule; gapped underlines under group headers; no vertical gridlines; unit line, as-of date, superscript footnotes and source line.

CSS gotchas: border-collapse:collapse plus position:sticky loses header borders, so use separate with border-spacing:0. Heat fills need print-color-adjust:exact to print. Use thead{display:table-header-group} and tr{break-inside:avoid} for paginated print, and unset sticky in print. CSS text-align:'.' is unsupported.

Heat colouring: compute the domain from non-target, non-NM values, clip at percentiles, diverge around the median for multiples (reversed for growth and margins), interpolate in OKLab/OKLCH with muted lightness, flip text to white on dark fills, always show a legend and make heat opt-in per column. Bake fills into XLSX on export.

In-cell micro-charts should be inline SVG (sparkline with last, min and max dots; two-sided data bars from a zero axis; bullet; 52-week range dot; win/loss), not one ECharts instance per cell. SVG stays vector in print and themes via currentColor.

Sensitivity tables (WACC x terminal growth, entry x exit multiple to IRR) are trivial in HTML: boxed base case, optional diverging fill vs current price. Optionally make them live via an rk.expr formula plus axis steppers to show dynamic re-rendering.

Table motion should be restrained: FLIP row reorder on sort and filter (~240ms), cross-fade recomputed stats, data bars growing on first reveal with stagger capped near 400ms, colour transitions on heat changes. No count-up on dense numeric tables. Honour prefers-reduced-motion and disable all motion in print.

Define tables via a declarative JSON TableSpec (columns and groups, fmt, NM rules, expr calculated columns, stats rows with exclude rule, heat, cell types, footnotes, export, interactions). It renders through RK.Table, can be adapted to Tabulator, AG Grid or S2, and gives a local LLM a safe target to edit (Step 2).

Licence traps to block in vendor.json review: HyperFormula (GPL-3.0), simple-datatables (LGPL-3.0), WebDataRocks (proprietary EULA, ~1 MB data cap), Handsontable (proprietary; only one 90-day evaluation for businesses), RevoGrid Pro, AG Grid Enterprise, Flexmonster. JSZip is dual MIT/GPL, so elect MIT.
